newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada said planning new telecom trade offer.
newsitem.headline: Canada said planning new telecom trade offer.

text.p: Facing a deadline in world telecommunications trade talks, Canada will make a new proposal on liberalizing its markets in the next two weeks, but will not go beyond its current offer to ease limits on foreign ownership of its phone companies, the Financial Post newspaper reported on Saturday.

The newspaper said Ottawa will offer to end the monopolies held by Telesat Canada on domestic satellite traffic and Teleglobe Canada on underseas cable telephone calls two years earlier than previously pledged.

But Canada will not raise the ceiling on foreign ownership of domestic phone companies beyond its offer of 46.7 percent. Current rules limit foreign carriers to a 20 percent direct and 33 percent indirect interest in Canadian phone companies.

The United States has been outspoken in demands that foreign ownership limits be raised, and acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said last week the U.S. wants a minimum 51 percent foreign ownership ceiling, the newspaper said.
The World Trade Organization talks face a February 15 deadline to reach a global accord on liberalizing telecommunications markets.

Officials in Ottawa were not available to comment on the report, which was attributed to unnamed sources. The newspaper said a federal cabinet committee would meet Tuesday to approve the latest offer which would be forwarded to Geneva in the next two weeks.

The domestic monopoly held by Telesat Canada, owned by BCE Inc, Spar Aerospace Ltd and phone companies, is due to expire in 2002 under Canada's current offer but that is being moved up to 2000 in the new offer. Teleglobe Canada's monopoly was to have expired in 1998 but that would be ended "almost immediately," the newspaper said.
